name: rh-proof-attempts
description: Curated local corpus of major documented RH proof-attempt families plus the OAE local reports used to compare literature routes against orchestrator routes.

bibliography.title: Zero-free regions and zero-density program
bibliography.note: Classical analytic work pushes zero-free regions toward the critical line and sharpens zero-density estimates.

bibliography.title: Mollifier and critical-line density methods
bibliography.note: Hardy, Selberg, Levinson, and Conrey style methods prove that many zeros lie on the critical line and improve the on-line proportion.

bibliography.title: Hilbert-Polya spectral operator program
bibliography.note: A self-adjoint operator with spectrum matching the imaginary parts of non-trivial zeros would force them onto the critical line.

bibliography.title: Connes and Bost-Connes noncommutative program
bibliography.note: Noncommutative geometry and zeta-partition-function dynamical systems aim to recast RH as a spectral statement.

bibliography.title: Pair-correlation and random-matrix heuristics
bibliography.note: Montgomery-Odlyzko style statistics suggest that zeta zeros behave like eigenvalues of GUE random matrices.

bibliography.title: Keiper-Li positivity criterion
bibliography.note: RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of the Li coefficients derived from log xi(s).

bibliography.title: Beurling-Nyman closure criterion
bibliography.note: RH is equivalent to a density or closure statement in L^2(0,1) for a specific function class.

bibliography.title: de Branges positivity and Hilbert-space program
bibliography.note: de Branges-style Hilbert spaces of entire functions aim to force RH through positivity and reproducing-kernel structure.

bibliography.title: de Bruijn-Newman flow and heat deformation
bibliography.note: RH is equivalent to the de Bruijn-Newman constant satisfying Lambda <= 0 under a heat-flow deformation of Xi.

bibliography.title: Polya-Jensen hyperbolicity program
bibliography.note: RH is equivalent to hyperbolicity of all relevant Jensen polynomials, and recent work proves wide finite-shift regimes.

bibliography.title: Turan route via Dirichlet polynomials
bibliography.note: Turan-type criteria try to deduce RH from zero-free properties of finite zeta partial sums or Dirichlet polynomials.

bibliography.title: Explicit-formula and positivity route
bibliography.note: Weil-style explicit formulas and positivity criteria tie prime sums to zero distributions with theorem-level exactness.

bibliography.title: Hardy Z and computational verification lane
bibliography.note: Hardy Z evaluations, Riemann-Siegel methods, and large-scale computation verify vast initial zero ranges on the critical line.

bibliography.title: Geometric and modulus-monotonicity route
bibliography.note: Visual and geometric interpretations study modulus flow, horizontal monotonicity, and critical-strip structure as a guide to zero geometry.
